classification.difficultyReason: Convert verbal journeys into signed velocity graphs, distinguishing a sustained stop from a zero crossing of the road-direction velocity component during a continuous U-turn.

inlines.text: For each of the scenarios below, sketch a possible velocity–time graph on a separate set of axes.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A delivery van moves off from rest, drives forwards towards a roundabout at a steady speed, negotiates a continuous U-turn around the roundabout without stopping, and exits along the original road in the opposite direction.

answer.short: A possible graph starts at zero, rises to a steady positive velocity, crosses the time axis during the continuous U-turn, then levels off below it.
answer.worked: Velocity is positive while the van travels forwards and negative when it returns along the road. The graph changes continuously through zero during the U-turn; this does not mean the van comes to a complete stop.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 31; answer-book PDF page 55, printed page 633
spec.description: Possible velocity–time graph: starts at zero, reaches a positive plateau, changes continuously through zero, then reaches a negative plateau.
spec.mathematics: The sign of velocity changes from positive to negative. The zero crossing represents a zero component along the chosen road direction during the U-turn.

children.label: b
children.prompt: A taxi pulls away from the kerb, drives towards a roundabout, comes to a complete stop at the give-way line, then enters the roundabout and performs a U-turn before continuing back along the same road.

answer.short: A possible graph starts at zero, rises above the time axis, returns to zero for the stop, rises above it again, then crosses below it during the U-turn.
answer.worked: The taxi first has positive velocity, then zero velocity while stopped at the give-way line. After moving forwards again, its signed velocity changes to negative as it turns and travels back along the road.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 32; answer-book PDF page 55, printed page 633
spec.description: Possible velocity–time graph: positive motion, a complete stop at zero, positive motion again, then a change to negative motion.
spec.mathematics: The zero interval represents the stop at the give-way line; the later change of sign represents the U-turn.
